README.txt.author: System
README.txt.content:
LEVEL 1: WHERE IS MY CYCLE??

You are a student at IIT Ropar and you have been alloted Chenab hostel
One day you wake up and find your cycle missing... 'Where did the thief take my cycle to?? Welcome to IIT Ropar BRUH'.

Your cycle has gone missing, and you decide to look for your cycle OUTSIDE CHENAB HOSTEL.

Objective: Locate your missing cycle by piecing together inconsistent logs and environmental clues.
Answer in the command line by using 'submit <passcode>'
Useful Commands:
- ls
- ls -a
- cd
- cat
- pwd
- grep

Helpful Senior.txt.author: Senior Rahul
Helpful Senior.txt.content:
You are not the first fresher to lose something within the first week, and you will not be the last. The important thing to understand is that memory on this campus is unreliable when you are tired, so always verify locations with more than one source.

If someone tells you they saw your cycle, treat it as a lead, not a fact. I have personally seen students argue over the location of the same object while standing in front of it.

Suspicious Freshie.txt.author: Anon Freshie
Suspicious Freshie.txt.content:
There is something strange about how people describe movement here. They don’t just say something was moved, they say it was ‘seen elsewhere’ as if distance itself is unreliable.

I am not involved in your cycle problem, but I would strongly suggest checking whether your assumption about where you parked it is even correct.

Mess Rumor.txt.author: Mess Attendant
Mess Rumor.txt.content:
A boy came into mess claiming his cycle was following him. You told him cycles do not have legs, but he insisted it stopped when he stopped and moved when he looked away.

Students are under too much stress during orientation, so you do not take these claims seriously, but you do write them down because patterns sometimes matter more than truth.

Lost Keys.txt.author: Warden Office
Lost Keys.txt.content: Key collection matching cycle lock number C-214 is unclaimed. Found in hostel lounge. Please collect if yours.

Gossip Corner.txt.author: Wing 3 Groupchat
Gossip Corner.txt.content: Some guy was seen locking his cycle at Chenab and walking all the way here into Brahmaputra. Sleepwalking is real guys, the first month is really exhausting and makes you do stuff!

log 23 06.txt.author: Security
log 23 06.txt.content:
22:00 - Routine verification completed with no anomalies reported at first glance.
23:30 - One subject observed near Cycle Row C behaving as if searching for a missing key, but no lost item was registered.
02:00 - Patrol completed, however sensor calibration shows minor drift in positional mapping data across two stands.

empty spot.txt.author: System
empty spot.txt.content: A faint circular imprint remains where a cycle once stood, but the soil compression pattern suggests it was not lifted vertically. Instead, it appears to have been rotated and reoriented before removal.

camera fragment.txt.author: Security AI
camera fragment.txt.content:
CCTV fragment shows a moving silhouette at 01:58 AM. The figure pauses longer than expected, as if verifying alignment with something unseen.

The footage suffers a brief timestamp reset, and during that interval, the object of interest is no longer visible in the frame.

Watchman Paaji.txt.content:

Either I am seeing too many nights or this place is playing tricks with records.

night patrol notes.txt.author: Night Guard
night patrol notes.txt.content:
Multiple cycle positions appear to shift slightly between patrol rounds without physical interference detected. Lighting conditions were stable, yet recorded coordinates do not always match visual confirmation.

This inconsistency has repeated across multiple nights and is now being flagged as a low-priority anomaly.

maintenance log.txt.author: Staff
maintenance log.txt.content: Cycle stand alignment was corrected near the central utility corridor after repeated misplacement complaints. No official unclaimed cycles were recorded today, though one lock mechanism without matching registry data was recovered and stored for inspection.

lost and found note.txt.author: Storekeeper
lost and found note.txt.content:
A freshly cut cycle lock was found near the juice stall area. It shows no signs of rust damage, suggesting recent removal rather than abandonment.

The item has been tagged as ‘unverified origin’ and placed under observation until ownership can be confirmed.

archive glitch log.txt.author: Library System
archive glitch log.txt.content:
A temporary catalog mismatch occurred during midnight synchronization, resulting in duplicate entries for several student records.

One of the entries referenced a blue cycle checkout request that was never submitted through official channels.

quiet floor note.txt.author: Librarian
quiet floor note.txt.content:
Students have reported hearing movement in the cycle stand area despite no visible activity. These reports increase during exam weeks, so they are usually attributed to fatigue.

However, the frequency of such reports this semester is unusually high.

map sync error.log.author: System Admin
map sync error.log.content:
Campus mapping system failed to reconcile coordinate data between Cycle Stand zones and Hostel allocation grid. Two distinct locations were assigned identical identifiers during synchronization.

This resulted in temporary overlap of Brahmaputra and Chenab mapping nodes.

node history.txt.author: System Admin
node history.txt.content:
Node tracking shows repeated reclassification of Cycle Stand C across different hostel zones. The system does not retain earlier mappings once overwritten, making historical reconstruction incomplete.

Recommendation: manual verification required for all cycle-related queries.
